collection.credit:
NEW EVENTS — PONDERING HOW LIFE HAS GONE (LIF-01..50, draft for the owner, 2026-11-15)
Adults of every age looking at their own lives so far: roads not taken, quiet satisfaction, small regrets, unexpected pride, things left unfinished, luck, gratitude and plenty of amusement. Nobody has to reach a verdict.
Written in the style of the owner's own events. Edit anything and send it back; nothing ships until you approve.

ledger.why: the casting line, carried out as the roles' ages (picks an adult aged 35 or older)

collection.description: A villager passes the hut of someone who once forgave them: leave flowers on the step, or just remember.

setup.name: The setup
setup.text: Years ago, (name1) did something careless that hurt someone badly. It wasn't on purpose, but it was (his/her) fault, and (he/she) knew it. The person forgave (him/her). Not right away, and not easily, but they did. Today, walking past their hut, (name1) remembers that, and stops for a moment.

o2.name: Outcome B
o2.text: (name1) doesn't do anything. (He/she) just stands there for a moment, remembering how it felt to be forgiven when (he/she) didn't expect to be. It changed (him/her). (He/she) is more careful now. Slower to blame other people. Quicker to say sorry. (He/she) walks on. The person inside the hut never knows (he/she) stopped.

o1__fx.name: Outcome A
o1__fx.text: (name1) picks a few flowers and leaves them on the step, without knocking. It's not an apology; (he/she) made that years ago. It's not a thank-you exactly. It's just a way of saying (he/she) hasn't forgotten what it meant. (He/she) doesn't know if they'll understand. (He/she) walks on, feeling a little lighter.
